title: A frown that the Quran chose to record.
subtitle: Small reactions are seen and weighed

row.title: just a face
sub: he could not even see it

row.title: a real turning away
sub: Allah saw it and named it

then: The Prophet ﷺ was speaking with one of the great leaders of Quraysh, hoping he would accept Islam. Ibn Umm Maktum, a blind man and an early Muslim, came asking about the faith. {trap}The Prophet ﷺ frowned and turned toward the leader.{/trap} The surah opens by naming that moment.
now: You are on a call with an important client when your younger brother walks in with a question. You do not say anything rude. You just give him a look and turn your chair. {idea}That small turn is a choice too.{/idea}
old: A look on my face is not really an action.
new: Allah counts even the frown and the turned shoulder.
try: Today, when someone interrupts you, turn your face fully toward them for a moment before answering.

title: The reason given: the blind man came.
subtitle: The person who seemed like an interruption
then: Aishah reported that Ibn Umm Maktum came saying, {reward}guide me{/reward}, while a leader of the idolaters sat with the Prophet ﷺ. The verse names him only as the blind man. {idea}The one who could not see is the one the surah defends.{/idea}
now: The intern who asks a basic question during the important meeting. The elderly neighbour who calls when you are rushing out. The child who tugs your sleeve. {trap}They feel like interruptions.{/trap} Sometimes they are the reason you are there.
old: This person is getting in the way of something important.
new: The person in front of me, asking sincerely, may be the important thing.
try: Notice the next person you label as an interruption today, and give them two full minutes.

title: You cannot see who is about to grow.
subtitle: Hidden potential in the overlooked person
then: Allah asks the Prophet ﷺ how he could know. Ibn Kathir explains it means the man {reward}may attain purification and cleanliness in his soul.{/reward} The leader seemed the bigger prize, but {idea}the real growth was waiting in the quiet seeker.{/idea}
now: You coach a youth team and give your attention to the two kids who already play well. The shy one in the back asks how to hold the ball. {idea}You have no idea what that question might turn into.{/idea}
old: I can judge who will benefit most from my time.
new: I cannot see who is about to change. Allah can.
try: Answer one question today from someone you would usually skip, as carefully as you would for anyone.

title: One reminder might have changed his life.
subtitle: The value of a word given to the willing
then: The verse continues the question: perhaps he would be reminded, and the reminder would help him. Ibn Kathir says it means {reward}he may receive admonition and abstain from the forbidden.{/reward} {idea}He came ready to listen.{/idea}
now: Your friend messages late at night: I think I want to pray again, where do I start? You are tired and reply with a thumbs up. {idea}A short honest answer now might be the one that sticks.{/idea}
old: A quick answer to a small question does not matter much.
new: A reminder given to someone who asked can change their whole path.
try: Reply properly to one question about faith or life that you have been leaving on read.

title: The man who felt he needed nothing.
subtitle: Self-sufficiency as a closed door
then: The leader sitting with the Prophet ﷺ was one of the great men of Quraysh. Ibn Kathir calls him the one who {trap}thinks himself self-sufficient.{/trap} He had wealth and status, and so felt no need for what was being offered.
now: You have the salary, the car, the healthy parents. When someone mentions Allah, you nod politely and check your phone. {trap}Nothing is wrong, so nothing feels needed.{/trap} That feeling is the thing the verse names.
old: I am doing fine, so I do not really need reminders.
new: Feeling I need nothing is exactly what closes me to guidance.
try: Make one honest dua today that starts with: O Allah, I need You for this.

title: Attention flowed toward the one who did not want it.
subtitle: Where our attention naturally goes
then: Ibn Kathir explains the meaning: {idea}you face the rich person so that perhaps he may be guided.{/idea} The Prophet's ﷺ hope was good, yet Allah pointed out that the eager attention was going to the one who showed no need.
now: At the family gathering you spend the evening impressing the uncle with connections. Your quiet cousin, who wanted to talk about something hard, leaves early. {trap}Our attention follows status without asking us.{/trap}
old: It makes sense to focus on the people who can do the most.
new: My attention should follow sincerity, not status.
try: At your next gathering, seek out the person who is sitting alone and talk with them first.

title: His refusal is not your burden.
subtitle: You deliver; guidance belongs to Allah
then: Ibn Kathir reads it as: {idea}you are not responsible for him if he does not attain purification.{/idea} Allah commanded the Prophet ﷺ to warn the noble and the weak equally, and then Allah guides whomever He chooses.
now: You keep chasing one relative with long messages, hoping to change their mind, while your own kids get your leftover patience. {idea}Your job is to say it well and kindly. The result is not yours to carry.{/idea}
old: If they do not change, it means I failed.
new: I am asked to convey and be fair. Guidance is in Allah's hands.
try: Let go of one argument you keep trying to win, and make dua for that person instead.

title: He came running, by his own will.
subtitle: The effort of the one who seeks
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {reward}he is seeking you and he comes to you so that he may be guided by what you say.{/reward} A blind man in Makkah had made his way to the Prophet ﷺ. {idea}No one sent him. He came.{/idea}
now: A new colleague keeps showing up early to ask how things work. A teenager at the masjid stays behind after the talk. {reward}Their effort is a kind of knocking.{/reward} It is easy to miss when you are busy.
old: People who keep asking are just being needy.
new: Someone who comes to me striving deserves my best attention.
try: Thank one person today for coming to you with a question, then answer it fully.

title: He came with fear of Allah in his heart.
subtitle: The inner state behind the question
then: The verse describes Ibn Umm Maktum as one who {idea}fears{/idea} while he strives toward the Prophet ﷺ. The leader felt self-sufficient. The blind man came afraid for his soul. {reward}Allah looked at the heart, not the rank.{/reward}
now: Two people message you about a lecture. One wants to argue for fun. One writes, I am scared I am getting this wrong. {idea}The second message carries something precious.{/idea} It deserves a slower reply.
old: I judge people mostly by how important they look.
new: The fear of Allah in someone's heart is what makes them weighty.
try: Before you reply to someone today, ask yourself what they might be feeling, not who they are.

title: Too busy for the one who truly came.
subtitle: Distraction from what matters most
then: Ibn Kathir sums it up in two words: {trap}you are too busy.{/trap} Here Allah commands His Messenger ﷺ not to single anyone out. {idea}The warning is for the noble and the weak, the rich and the poor, the young and the old alike.{/idea}
now: Your daughter is telling you about her day while you answer emails. You say mm-hm three times. {trap}You were there, but not with her.{/trap} The verse asks who you were really busy with.
old: I can half-listen now and give full attention later.
new: Being too busy for a sincere person is a loss I may not get back.
try: Put your phone face down for one conversation today and listen until the person is finished.

title: No. This is a reminder, not a privilege.
subtitle: The message is for everyone equally
then: The surah turns with a firm {trap}No!{/trap} Ibn Kathir says the reminder refers to this surah, or to {idea}the advice of conveying knowledge equally among people, whether noble or low class.{/idea} Qatadah and As-Suddi said it means the Quran.
now: Your study circle quietly becomes a club for the articulate ones. The cleaner at your office never gets invited. {idea}The Quran was never meant to have a guest list.{/idea}
old: Some people are more suited to religious knowledge than others.
new: The reminder belongs equally to everyone who will listen.
try: Share one verse or good word today with someone you would not normally talk to about faith.

title: Whoever wants it can take it.
subtitle: The door is open, the choice is yours
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {reward}whoever wills, he remembers Allah in all of his affairs.{/reward} After the scene with the chief and the blind man, the point is clear. {idea}No one is pushed in and no one is kept out.{/idea}
now: You keep waiting to feel more qualified, more pious, less busy before you open the Quran. {idea}The verse only asks one thing: do you want it?{/idea} The app is already on your phone.
old: I am not the kind of person who is really religious.
new: The reminder is open to me the moment I choose it.
try: Read one page of Quran today, at whatever pace you can.

title: Written on pages held in honor.
subtitle: The dignity of what you are reading
then: Ibn Kathir says {reward}all of the Quran is in honored pages, meaning respected and revered.{/reward} The leader of Quraysh did not need to accept it for it to matter. {idea}Its honor came from Allah, not from any audience.{/idea}
now: You hesitate to mention the Quran at work because it might seem uncool. {idea}Its worth does not rise or fall with anyone's reaction in the break room.{/idea} It was honored before you opened it.
old: The message matters more when important people accept it.
new: The Quran is honored by Allah, whoever accepts or ignores it.
try: Handle your Quran or open the app today with one moment of deliberate respect before reading.

title: Raised high and kept pure.
subtitle: Nothing added, nothing missing
then: Ibn Kathir explains the two words: exalted means {reward}elevated in status{/reward}, and purified means {idea}free from impurity, additions and deficiency.{/idea} This is the reminder the proud chief turned away from.
now: Your feed is full of edited clips, rumors, and posts that change every hour. {idea}Then there is one text that has not been bent.{/idea} You can open it at the bus stop.
old: Everything I read is shaped by someone's agenda.
new: The Quran is kept high and clean, a steady thing in a noisy world.
try: Swap five minutes of scrolling today for five minutes with the Quran.
